q: The F2 phenotypic ratio obtained in a monohybrid cross according to Mendel's laws is:
why: Monohybrid cross F2 gives 3 dominant : 1 recessive ratio.

q: A dihybrid cross following independent assortment gives an F2 ratio of:
why: Two independently assorting gene pairs give the classic 9:3:3:1 ratio.

q: Crossing over, which produces recombinant gametes, occurs during:
why: Crossing over between homologous chromosomes happens at prophase I of meiosis.

q: Morgan's classic linkage experiments demonstrating linked genes used which organism?
why: Morgan studied linkage between body colour and wing shape genes in Drosophila.

q: In humans, the sex of a child is determined by the chromosome carried by the:
why: The egg always carries X; sperm carries X or Y, so the father determines sex.

q: In the bird ZW sex-determination system, males have the genotype:
why: In birds, males are ZZ and females are ZW, reversed from the human XY system.

q: An X-linked recessive disorder like haemophilia appears mostly in:
why: Recessive X-linked traits show up mainly in males since they have only one X allele.

q: A karyotype of 47 chromosomes with trisomy of chromosome 21 indicates:
why: Down syndrome is caused by an extra copy (trisomy) of chromosome 21.

q: A child with blood group AB has genotype IAIB, which demonstrates the concept of:
why: Both IA and IB alleles express together (both antigens present), showing codominance.
